Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: My father narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us (Abdullah said: "I heard it from him myself"), Marwan ibn Mu'awiya al-Fazari narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ta'ifi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Abi Jabal al-Udwani, from his father, that he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the cattle-pen of Thaqif, standing on a bow or a staff, when he came to them seeking their support. He heard him recite: "By the sky and the night-comer," until he finished the surah. He said: "I memorised it during the Jahiliyyah while I was a polytheist, and then I recited it in Islam." He said: "Thaqif then summoned me and said: 'What did you hear from this man?' I recited it to them. Those from Quraysh who were with them said: 'We know our companion better. If we knew that what he says is true, we would have followed him.'" [Al-Musnad (4/335). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/136): "Abd al-Rahman was mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim, and no one has recorded him, but the rest of his narrators are trustworthy."]

And al-Nasa'i said: Amr ibn Mansur narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Jabir, who said: Mu'adh prayed the Maghrib prayer and recited al-Baqarah and al-Nisa'. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Are you causing trouble, O Mu'adh? Would it not have sufficed you to recite 'By the sky and the night-comer,' and 'By the sun and its brightness,' and similar surahs?" [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11664.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Allah swears by the sky and what He placed in it of shining stars. Therefore He says: ﴿By the sky and the night-comer﴾. Then He says: ﴿And what will make you know what the night-comer is?﴾ Then He explained it by saying: ﴿It is the piercing star.﴾

Qatada and others said: The star was only called "night-comer" (tariq) because it is seen at night and hidden by day. This is supported by the authentic hadith in which he forbade a man to come upon his family suddenly (turuq), that is, to come to them unexpectedly at night. [Al-Bukhari, no. 5243, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.] And in another hadith containing a supplication: "Except a night-comer who comes with good, O Most Merciful." [Ahmad, al-Musnad (3/419), from Abd al-Rahman ibn Khanbash, may Allah be pleased with him.]

* *

As for His words ﴿the piercing (al-thaqib)﴾: Ibn Abbas said: "the shining one." Al-Suddi said: "It pierces the devils when it is sent against them." Ikrimah said: "It is shining and burns the devil."

* *

As for His words ﴿There is no soul but that it has over it a guardian﴾: that is, every soul has over it a guardian from Allah who protects it from calamities, as He says: ﴿For him there are successive angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of Allah﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11].

* *

As for His words ﴿So let man consider from what he was created﴾: this is a reminder to man of the weakness of his origin from which he was created, and a guidance for him to acknowledge the Resurrection, for whoever is able to originate creation is all the more able to restore it, as He says: ﴿And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27].

* *

As for His words ﴿He was created from a gushing fluid﴾: this means the semen, which is ejected forcefully from the man and the woman, and from them the child is produced by the permission of Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic. Therefore He says: ﴿It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs﴾, meaning the backbone of the man and the ribs (al-taraʾib) of the woman, which is her chest.

Shabib ibn Bishr narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs﴾: the backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman, yellowish and thin; the child is only produced from the two of them. Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, Qatada, al-Suddi, and others.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usama narrated to us, from Mis'ar: I heard al-Hakam mention from Ibn Abbas: ﴿It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs﴾, and he said: "These are the ribs," and he placed his hand on his chest.

Al-Dahhak and Atiyya said, from Ibn Abbas: the taraʾib of the woman is the place of the necklace. Likewise said Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Ali ibn Abi Talha said, from Ibn Abbas: the taraʾib is between her two breasts.

From Mujahid: the taraʾib is what lies between the two shoulders to the chest. Also from him: the taraʾib is below the collarbones (al-taraqi). Sufyan al-Thawri said: above the two breasts. From Sa'id ibn Jubayr: the taraʾib are four ribs on this lower side.

From al-Dahhak: the taraʾib is between the two breasts, the two legs, and the two eyes.

Al-Layth ibn Sa'd said, from Ma'mar ibn Abi Habiba al-Madani, that it reached him concerning the saying of Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic: ﴿It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs﴾, that he said: "It is the essence of the heart; from there the child comes."

From Qatada: ﴿It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs﴾: from between his backbone and his chest.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, He is Able to return him﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: He is able to return this gushing fluid to the place from which it emerged. This was said by Mujahid, Ikrimah, and others.

The second: He is able to return this human being created from a gushing fluid, that is, to restore him and resurrect him for the Hereafter, because whoever is able to originate creation is able to restore it. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned this proof in the Qur'an in several places. This view was held by al-Dahhak and chosen by Ibn Jarir. Therefore He says: ﴿On the Day when secrets are examined﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, secrets will be examined, meaning they will be exposed and made apparent, and what was hidden will become open and well known. It is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "For every treacherous person a banner will be raised at his buttocks, and it will be said: 'This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3188; Sahih Muslim, no. 1735.]

* *

As for His words ﴿Then he will have no power﴾, that is, man on the Day of Resurrection ﴿and no helper﴾, that is, from outside himself: he will not be able to rescue himself from the punishment of Allah, and no one will be able to do that for him.
